name: NFT Trader BatchSwap counterparty reentrancy
summary: BatchSwap.closeSwapIntent() settles the creator's side of a swap with an ERC-721 safeTransferFrom before the counterparty side, and has no reentrancy guard. The attacker re-entered from onERC721Received and called editCounterPart() to point the open swap at any address that still held an ERC-721 approval to the contract, so settlement then pulled that address's token to the attacker.

loss.notes: 143 distinct NFTs were pulled from approval-holding victims through this contract between blocks 18797420 and 18799856. Only the 12 BAYC and 13 MAYC are valued. Unit values are the median single-item marketplace fill for each collection over blocks 18790000-18804000, taken only from transactions carrying a Seaport OrderFulfilled or Blur execution event and measured as the payment received by the seller, with every campaign address excluded: BAYC 26.300 ETH from 34 sales, MAYC 5.190 ETH from 85 sales. Those medians are converted at the DefiLlama ETH price for the incident timestamp. The remaining 118 NFTs across 25 collections (World of Women, Hashmasks, HERO, VeeFriends, 0N1, HAPE, OCMonk, CloneX, PartyBears, Azuki, Doodles and others) are not valued, so the figure is a conservative floor; press coverage of the whole NFT Trader event reports close to USD 3 million across both exploited swap contracts. The 26 BAYC and 9 MAYC taken through the separate contract 0x13d8faf4a690f5ae52e2d2c52938d1167057b9af are recorded under eip155:1:0x906d06acd236c48a8c8708d7dc50d968b8faad7c7c393e7c01549adf4922b180 and are not counted here. Recovery is excluded: Yuga Labs and Boring Security later paid a 120 ETH bounty and the main exploiter returned 36 BAYC and 18 MAYC.

lastCodeChange.description: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0xf47d9ba7a1d6818b73b3936ee83e718ad4f2e24e6d14a1b93d856c6ded1dcb16 both at the deployment block 12505457 and at block 18797419, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

sources.note: Re-anchored. The v1 snapshot anchored this record to 0xec7523660f, which is a later transaction of the same campaign sent by a copycat exploiter. Enumerating every transaction that emitted a log from 0xc310e760778ecbca4c65b6c559874757a4c4ece0 between blocks 18790000 and 18810000 and keeping only ERC-721 transfers whose sender is neither the transaction sender nor its entry contract yields 143 distinct victim tokens and identifies 0x431341c6d4 at block 18797420 as the earliest transaction that pulls a victim token; four distinct exploiters used the same path, the first being 0xd717b85b5d through 0xc446e0a1e2. The trace of the anchor shows closeSwapIntent settling the creator leg first, the attacker re-entering from onERC721Received to call editCounterPart, and the counterparty leg then transferring the victim's BAYC. The contract is not upgradeable: its runtime code hash is 0xf47d9ba7a1d6818b73b3936ee83e718ad4f2e24e6d14a1b93d856c6ded1dcb16 at both the deployment block and block 18797419, and its EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so age runs from the 2021-05-25 deployment by 0x4bc2f1e9bf517cd944e8ffe0047c80c5b574d532, 934.5 days. Collection medians used for valuation come from single-item marketplace fills over blocks 18790000-18804000, restricted to transactions carrying a Seaport or Blur fill event and measured as the seller-side payment, excluding every campaign address. An earlier revision of this record used a looser sampler that counted any transfer accompanied by a WETH movement and returned a BAYC median of 21.801 ETH; that sample included non-sale transfers and understated the floor, and the corrected medians are BAYC 26.300 ETH and MAYC 5.190 ETH.
